title: Blood tests
intended_use: Support general blood test questions, blood draw expectations, result timing, needle anxiety, and result follow-up.
safety_boundary: Do not infer diagnosis from a blood test alone; results can be complicated and should be discussed with a healthcare professional.
notes: Existing NHS blood test coverage is already present; review overlap before drafting new KB items.

title: What You Need to Know About Blood Testing
intended_use: Support general checkup and common blood-test explainer questions without product-first wording.
safety_boundary: Use as general education only; do not claim a generic panel is sufficient for diagnosis or screening for every person.
notes: Review against existing NHS blood-tests source to avoid duplicate KB items.

title: How to Prepare for a Lab Test
intended_use: Support fasting, medicine disclosure, supplements, and provider instruction questions before lab testing.
safety_boundary: Preparation varies by test and person; users should follow instructions from their provider or lab and should not stop medicines unless told.
notes: Useful for glucose, lipid, creatinine, and general preparation cases.

title: How to Understand Your Lab Results
intended_use: Anchor result-boundary responses about reference ranges, lab-to-lab differences, trends, and clinician interpretation.
safety_boundary: HomeLab must not diagnose from result values; advise review with a healthcare professional using symptoms, history, medicines, and lab reference ranges.
notes: Primary source for medical review boundary items.

title: Laboratory Tests
intended_use: Support broad lab-test role explanations for screening, monitoring, diagnosis support, and routine checkups.
safety_boundary: Lab results should be interpreted by a health professional and compared with context and prior results.
notes: Good supporting source for broad test advice and clarification cases.

title: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
intended_use: Support CBC meaning, anemia and infection clues, blood cell components, and CBC result-boundary cases.
safety_boundary: CBC is one tool; diagnosis requires medical history, symptoms, and other factors.
notes: Existing source family is already used in v1.3; Batch 4A can strengthen result-boundary wording.

title: Blood Count Tests
intended_use: Support broader blood count test explanations around anemia, infection, clotting problems, and immune disorders.
safety_boundary: Do not diagnose anemia, infection, cancer, or immune disorders from CBC alone.
notes: Use as a secondary CBC overview source.

title: C-Reactive Protein (CRP) Test
intended_use: Support CRP as an inflammation marker and infection-oriented test advice with limitations.
safety_boundary: CRP can indicate inflammation but does not show the exact cause or location; provider must interpret with symptoms and other tests.
notes: Useful for infection-related test advice and known v1.3 retrieval gaps.

title: Blood culture
intended_use: Support blood culture explanations for suspected infection contexts alongside CBC and CRP.
safety_boundary: Blood culture is ordered and interpreted by clinicians; do not recommend it as routine package screening or delay urgent care.
notes: Existing v1.3 source family; keep urgent infection safety priority.

title: Blood Glucose Test
intended_use: Support fasting glucose, random glucose, routine checkup glucose, symptom context, and fasting preparation questions.
safety_boundary: High or low glucose may indicate problems but must be interpreted with test type, other tests, history, and clinician review.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test
intended_use: Support HbA1c meaning, average glucose over time, no-fasting distinction, screening, monitoring, and follow-up testing.
safety_boundary: Do not declare diabetes from one result in HomeLab; abnormal results require provider review and sometimes confirmatory testing.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: Diabetes Tests & Diagnosis
intended_use: Support differences between A1C, fasting plasma glucose, random plasma glucose, and oral glucose tolerance testing.
safety_boundary: Do not self-diagnose; diagnosis should be made by a doctor, often with repeat or confirmatory testing.
notes: Authoritative NIDDK source for diabetes test boundaries.

title: Cholesterol Levels
intended_use: Support lipid panel contents, LDL, HDL, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and cardiovascular risk context.
safety_boundary: Cardiovascular risk and treatment decisions require clinician review and full risk profile, not a single value.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: Triglycerides Test
intended_use: Support triglyceride-specific eval cases and explain triglycerides as part of a lipid profile.
safety_boundary: High triglycerides do not automatically define a specific disease; provider interprets with cholesterol, risk factors, and history.
notes: Complements cholesterol source for lipid panel coverage.

title: Liver Function Tests
intended_use: Support liver function test, ALT, AST, bilirubin, abnormal result, and liver-test follow-up questions.
safety_boundary: Elevated ALT, AST, or bilirubin does not by itself diagnose hepatitis, cirrhosis, or alcohol-related disease; provider interpretation is needed.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3; manually verify marker-specific wording before drafting KB items.

title: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
intended_use: Support broad metabolic panel questions spanning glucose, liver, kidney, electrolyte, and routine checkup contexts.
safety_boundary: CMP gives clues about overall physical health but abnormal values need follow-up and professional interpretation.
notes: Bridge source for combined liver, kidney, and glucose user questions.

title: Creatinine Test
intended_use: Support creatinine, blood and urine creatinine, eGFR calculation, UACR relationship, and kidney-health interpretation.
safety_boundary: Creatinine alone is not the best measure of kidney function; eGFR, UACR, and clinical context matter.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) Test
intended_use: Support eGFR meaning, kidney filtering, creatinine-based calculation, and routine kidney screening.
safety_boundary: eGFR should be interpreted by a provider with age, sex, creatinine, urine tests, medical history, and repeat testing as needed.
notes: Pairs with creatinine source for kidney function explanation.

title: Kidney Tests
intended_use: Support overview of kidney tests including GFR, creatinine, urine albumin, urinalysis, and imaging context.
safety_boundary: HomeLab should not diagnose kidney disease; kidney tests require professional interpretation and often multiple measures.
notes: Good overview source for kidney-related recommendation/test-advice answers.

title: Urinalysis
intended_use: Support urinalysis explanation, urine protein, glucose, ketones, bilirubin, bacteria, kidney, UTI, and diabetes contexts.
safety_boundary: Urinalysis abnormalities are not diagnosis; they must be interpreted with symptoms, urine culture or other tests, and clinician review.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio
intended_use: Support urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, kidney damage screening, diabetes kidney monitoring, and follow-up with eGFR.
safety_boundary: Abnormal UACR usually needs repeat or follow-up kidney testing and clinician interpretation.
notes: Supports diabetes and kidney monitoring eval cases.

title: Albuminuria: Albumin in the Urine
intended_use: Support albuminuria explanation, urine dipstick vs urine albumin-creatinine measurement, and kidney disease monitoring context.
safety_boundary: Do not diagnose chronic kidney disease from a single urine albumin result; provider review and often repeat testing are needed.
notes: Authoritative NIDDK kidney source.

title: Thyroid Tests
intended_use: Support thyroid test overview, TSH, T3, T4, antibodies, fatigue, weight, coldness, and thyroid test selection questions.
safety_boundary: Symptoms such as fatigue or weight change are nonspecific; thyroid diagnosis requires lab interpretation and clinical context.
notes: High-priority gap in v1.3.

title: TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone) Test
intended_use: Support TSH meaning, thyroid regulation, why TSH is ordered, and high or low TSH boundaries.
safety_boundary: TSH alone may not show the cause; providers may order T4, T3, antibody tests and interpret symptoms and history.
notes: Direct TSH source for thyroid eval cases.

title: Thyroxine (T4) Test
intended_use: Support T4 explanation, free vs total T4, and relationship between T4 and TSH.
safety_boundary: T4 alone is not enough to diagnose thyroid problems; interpret with TSH and clinical context.
notes: Complements TSH and thyroid overview sources.

title: Thyroid Tests
intended_use: Support thyroid diagnostic test overview including TSH, T4, T3, antibody tests, and symptom context.
safety_boundary: Do not diagnose thyroid disease from symptoms or a single lab marker; testing and interpretation should be done with healthcare professional review.
notes: Authoritative NIDDK source complementing MedlinePlus thyroid pages.
